plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers that bloom in the cool season. It is widely cultivated in gardens and also grows wild in woodlands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak in winter)
plants.location: Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant used to make all true tea, and camellia seed oil has been used in East Asia for centuries for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing perennial with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers with golden stamens that emerge in the depths of winter, often pushing through snow. It prefers shaded, calcareous woodland soils.
plants.location: Mountain woodlands of the Alps and northern Apennines in Europe; cultivated in temperate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a true rose; it belongs to the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with fern-like leaves and spectacular clusters of large flame-colored flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere summer, it puts on a fiery display.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February); also blooms in the tropics during the dry season
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including northern Australia, Brazil, and southern Africa
plants.funFact: This species is endangered in its native Madagascar even though it is one of the most commonly planted ornamental trees in the world.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bulbous perennial producing tall, hollow stalks topped by large trumpet-shaped flowers. Native plants flower in the tropical summer, while potted bulbs are forced to bloom indoors in northern winters.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter indoors in the Northern Hemisphere; summer in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to Central and South America and the Caribbean; grown worldwide as a houseplant
plants.funFact: Hippeastrum is often mistakenly called amaryllis, but the true Amaryllis genus is a different group native to South Africa.
